summary.text: The sperm whale is the largest toothed whale and the largest toothed predator, a pelagic mammal found throughout the world's oceans.
It dives as deep as 2,250 m, uses echolocation and calls as loud as 236 decibels underwater, the loudest of any animal, and has the largest brain on Earth.
Its head holds a waxy substance called spermaceti, a prime target of whalers for lamps and candles, and the species is now protected and listed as vulnerable.

facts.label: Brain size
facts.value: Over five times heavier than a human's

items.prompt: Where does the sperm whale's name actually come from?

options.label: Its unusually large numbers of offspring
A waxy head substance once mistaken for semen
A Latin word meaning 'great sea beast'
The tapering shape of its long body

items.explain: The name is short for 'spermaceti whale', after the waxy substance in its head that was originally mistaken for semen.

items.prompt: Underwater, how does the loudness of a sperm whale's sounds compare with other animals?

options.label: Quieter than most dolphins
About as loud as a seal
The loudest of any animal
Too faint for us to detect

items.explain: Its echolocation and calls reach 236 decibels underwater, the loudest of any animal.

items.prompt: What animal hunts a mature, healthy adult sperm whale?

options.label: Large great white sharks
Packs of giant squid
Polar bears at the ice edge
None; it has no natural predators

items.explain: A mature, healthy sperm whale has no natural predators, though orca pods sometimes kill calves and weakened adults.

items.prompt: A sperm whale calf is born into its group. Who looks after it?

options.label: Females who cooperate to guard and nurse it
Its father, who stays by the calf's side
Nobody, since calves fend for themselves
Older males who patrol around the group

items.explain: Females and young live together in groups, and the females cooperate to protect and nurse the young, while mature males live alone outside mating season.

items.prompt: Beachcombers watch for lumps of ambergris, a waxy waste from sperm whales' digestive systems. Why is it valued?

options.label: As a cooking fat
As a fixative in perfumes
As a building cement
As a crop fertilizer

items.explain: Ambergris is still highly valued as a fixative in perfumes, among other uses.

items.prompt: Its scientific name means 'big-headed'. In a mature male, how much of the body's length can the head make up?

options.label: Up to one-tenth
Up to one-fifth
Up to one-third
Up to three-quarters

items.explain: Mature males average about 16 m, with the head making up as much as one-third of that length.
